title: Ferdinand, King of Hungary and Bohemia (future Ferdinand III), to Maximilian von Trauttmansdorff, 13 November 1634 (SOA Plzeň, RA Trauttmansdorffů, kart. 6, inv. č. 68)

documents.shelfmark: SOA Plzeň, pracoviště Klášter u Nepomuka, Rodinný archiv Trauttmansdorffů, karton 6, inv. č. 68 (contemporary copy)
documents.route: Ferdinand, King of Hungary and Bohemia -> Maximilian von Trauttmansdorff

system.summary: Not seen. Mírka (2012, n. 39) describes the cipher alphabet as exclusively two- and three-digit numbers and takes it for a nomenclator with homophones, bigrams and probably codes.
system.notes: Ferdinand's cipher of 28 Oct 1634 (DECODE R1887, ferdinand3) is graphic signs plus three-letter codes, so it is not this system. Mírka suggests the key may be in Vienna (FA Trauttmansdorff, HHStA).

conditions.human_role: The user supplied the target (catalogue 359) and, after the online search failed, Mírka's 2012 offprint; the user asked to close it out unread.

solution.what: Re-pulled the full DECODE record list (10,106 records) and searched it for the Trauttmansdorff family archive: only inv. 200 (Kurz 1639) is there, not inv. 68.

Checked Cryptoole HUXXXX-1, Cryptiana's unsolved list, the SOA Plzeň publications page and Portaro library catalogue, and ResearchGate for an image of the letter or of Mírka's article: none online (the volume is print-only; ResearchGate behind a CAPTCHA).
Read Šimsová's 2024 thesis on Ferdinand III's cipher letters to Gallas (1635-38) for this letter or a 1634 numeric key: not mentioned; the Gallas key does not survive.

Read Mírka's 2012 offprint (supplied by the user): the item is a contemporary copy in a cipher of two- and three-digit numbers only, a nomenclator in his view; no figure of it; key possibly in Vienna.
Compared with Ferdinand's cipher of 28 Oct 1634 (DECODE R1887, rebuilt in ferdinand3): graphic signs and three-letter codes, not numbers, so it cannot be this letter's key.

outcome.method_basis: No image of the letter is online or in print, so the ciphertext was never seen; Mírka's description rules out the one known 1634 key of Ferdinand's (R1887).

gaps.detail: no image online or in print; scans must be ordered from SOA Plzeň (Klášter)

outcome.notes: Catalogue 359 stays open with outcome 'attempted, open'. Next: scans from SOA Plzeň; a numeric nomenclator of Ferdinand's 1634 correspondence in Vienna.
